note: Two offline planning scenarios for connection reuse, SQL execution choices, current saved-query limitations, and Airflow SDK deployment. Give a fresh evaluator the full skill and one prompt, without expected_output or assertions. Do not execute platform operations. Assess every assertion against the resulting answer; these cases require human or model judgement and do not prove live API behavior.

evals.name: transfer-discovery-and-saved-analysis
evals.prompt: We use DLP and already have a PostgreSQL connection in workbook Sources. Plan a Copy transfer into our lakehouse: discover the source tables and choose incremental cursors and initial values. The orders table has update_dt populated on every change; events is append-only with a monotonically increasing id; signups is append-only with create_dt. We need the full available history on the first load. I also want an ad-hoc SQL analysis saved in workbook Analysis using the existing connection. Explain the plan and any prerequisite for saving and running that analysis. Do not call APIs or change resources.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the configured connection for SQL inspection, choose the transfer table list and verified cursor values, and include the requested initial history. For the saved analysis, first copy or link the connection into Analysis, then save the query and run it by ID through runSqlQuery (or its documented SDK equivalent).

assertions.text: Uses the existing PostgreSQL connection to inspect tables, columns, and data through SQL before choosing the transfer table list; does not require a new direct database connection.
Selects update_dt for mutable orders and considers id and create_dt for the append-only tables.
Determines type-compatible initial cursor values from source inspection to include the full requested history, without guessing values or excluding the earliest rows.
Requires a copy of or link to the existing connection in Analysis before binding the saved SQL query to it.
Chooses a saved DataLens SQL query and /rpc/runSqlQuery by query ID, or the documented SDK equivalent; does not assume an external PostgreSQL connection supplies a Trino coordinator.

evals.name: git-etl-and-temporary-trino-sql
evals.prompt: We are setting up a reliable DLP Airflow ETL pipeline. SQL files will be reviewed and versioned in Git, and we do not want saved DataLens query objects for each run. We also need to execute an occasional temporary Trino diagnostic without saving it. Recommend how to discover the endpoint, authenticate, execute SQL, and know when downstream tasks can start. Our DAGs may be delivered from Git or S3, and their Python code needs the DataLens SDK to look up platform resources. Explain how to make the SDK available in either deployment. Do not call APIs or deploy anything.
evals.expected_output: Use the native Trino endpoint discovered through getTrinoCluster for both Git-managed ETL and unsaved diagnostics, authenticate with a Yandex Cloud IAM bearer token, and wait for terminal successful execution. Explain the current saved-query API limitation and make the SDK plus dependencies importable through the selected DAG deployment or supported package installation.

assertions.text: Chooses direct Trino execution for both Git-managed ETL and the temporary diagnostic; discovers coordinatorUrl through /rpc/getTrinoCluster or its documented SDK equivalent.
Specifies a Yandex Cloud IAM token in Authorization: Bearer for the Trino endpoint, without embedding or logging a real token.
Submits SQL via /v1/statement and follows nextUri until absent while checking errors, or uses a Trino client that does this; does not release downstream tasks on submission alone.
Explains that the public DataLens SQL-query API currently runs a saved query by ID and does not invent a raw-SQL argument or a temporary-query RPC.

Recommends making the DataLens SDK available with DAGs delivered from Git or S3, ensures dependencies and imports work in the parser and workers, and does not treat uploading an uninstalled archive as sufficient.
